chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Murazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has revealed in the Quran a clarification of everything, to the extent that, by God, Allah has not left out anything which the servants would be in need of, such that no servant is able to say, 'If only this (matter) had been revealed in the Quran,' except that Allah has already revealed it therein.

key_terms.أَنْزَلَ: Anzala — to send down/reveal; the technical term for divine revelation
key_terms.الْعِبَاد: Al-'ibad — 'the servants' (of God), referring to all of humanity who depend on divine guidance
key_terms.تِبْيَان: Tibyan — comprehensive clarification/explanation; a term indicating that the Quran does not merely hint but fully clarifies

ai.seo_question: Does the Quran contain guidance for every matter according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the comprehensive nature of the Quran as a divine guidance that addresses every need of humanity. This teaching, narrated through a chain reaching back to the Imam, underscores the Shia theological position that the Quran contains the answer to every matter of religion and life, whether explicitly or through the Imam's authoritative interpretation. The audience — students of religious law — would have understood this as establishing the Quran's sufficiency alongside the Sunnah and Imami teaching.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Murazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Revealed in the Quran an explanation of everything to the extent that, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not neglect anything which the servants would be needy to, until there is no capacity for a servant to be saying, ‘If only this (matter) had been Revealed in the Quran’, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Revealed in it’.
